expectations.text: Stream is exposed as a cold Flow returned from a NON-suspend function (not a `suspend fun` returning Flow), so collection stays lazy and cancellable
expectations.evidence: PriceWatchClient.kt:129-148 `public fun stream(symbol: String, onState): Flow<PriceTick>` — non-suspend, returns a cold `flow{}` (private `ticks`, l.151-163) wrapped in `.retryWhen{}`. KDoc l.104-106 states 'stream returns a cold Flow: nothing connects until a collector starts.'

expectations.text: Cancellation is correct: no swallowed CancellationException; clean shutdown happens via scope cancellation; no GlobalScope is used
expectations.evidence: PriceWatchClient.kt:194-196 `is CancellationException -> false` is the FIRST arm of `isTransient()`, so retryWhen's predicate returns false for cancellation and rethrows it (never retried/swallowed). No GlobalScope (grep clean). ViewModel collects with `launchIn(scope)` (PriceWatchViewModel.kt:38) so scope cancellation tears the stream down.

expectations.text: Retries ONLY transient failures (timeouts/5xx/transport) with capped + jittered exponential backoff; does not retry terminal 4xx; not a bare `while(true)` catch-all with no delay
expectations.evidence: PriceWatchClient.kt:137-147 uses `Flow.retryWhen` whose predicate calls `isTransient()` (l.194-215): 5xx (ServerResponseException / SSEClientException w/ 5xx status), HttpRequestTimeoutException, IOException => retry; 4xx (ClientRequestException, non-5xx SSEClientException) and SerializationException => give up. Backoff (ExponentialBackoff l.86-96) = `random.nextDouble() * min(base*2^(n-1), maxDelay)` — capped full jitter via injected delay. Test `does not retry permanent 4xx` asserts 404 => 1 call. No while(true). (Minor: 408/429 are treated as terminal since isTransientStatus is only 500..599, but the assertion's named transient cases — timeouts/5xx/transport — are all retried and 4xx is not retried.)

expectations.text: The HttpClient/engine and the dispatcher are INJECTED (constructor params) so the class is unit-testable (and any Clock/Random too)
expectations.evidence: PriceWatchClient.kt:116-122 constructor injects `httpClient`, `decoder`, `backoff`, `maxRetries` — but NO CoroutineDispatcher param. grep for 'dispatcher|flowOn|Dispatchers' across all without_skill outputs returns ZERO hits. The class never sets a dispatcher (no flowOn), so it cannot be pinned/swapped for testing on a TestDispatcher; tests rely solely on runTest's ambient scheduler. The assertion explicitly requires the dispatcher to be an injected constructor param, which it is not. (Random IS injectable via ExponentialBackoff; HttpClient is injected — but the dispatcher requirement is unmet.)

expectations.text: Does NOT return a fake or last-known value on failure that masks the outage (no silent fallback that fakes success)
expectations.evidence: PriceWatchClient.kt:140 retryWhen returns `false` on terminal/exhausted failure => rethrows to the collector; no fallback tick is emitted. ViewModel (PriceWatchViewModel.kt:37) routes the failure to `_error` StateFlow rather than synthesizing a price. No last-known/default value substituted.

expectations.text: Avoids constructing Json per-call and frames the stream incrementally (does not re-split an ever-growing accumulated buffer)
expectations.evidence: PriceWatchClient.kt:176-178 `JsonPriceTickDecoder(private val json: Json = Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true })` — the Json is a field built once per decoder instance, not constructed per decode() call. Framing is incremental via the Ktor SSE plugin `incoming.collect { event: ServerSentEvent -> event.data }` (l.158-161); the plugin yields discrete events, no accumulated-buffer re-split.

expectations.text: Stays at Tier 0 for this app-level task: does NOT impose published-API/ABI/explicitApi/publishing rules that don't apply
expectations.evidence: The deliverable imposes no ABI dump, no explicitApi() gating, no Maven Central/publishing requirements. transcript.md l.93-94 only NOTES 'public/explicitApi modifiers are present so this drops cleanly into a library module... harmless in an app module' — it volunteers compatibility rather than imposing publishing rules on the task. No binary-compat hazards flagged against the app code.

claims.claim: Ktor surfaces a failed SSE handshake as SSEClientException carrying the HttpResponse
claims.evidence: PriceWatchClient.kt:204 `is SSEClientException -> response?.status?.isTransientStatus()`; transcript notes this was confirmed against Ktor docs after an initial mistaken custom exception.

PriceWatchClient.kt:217 `isTransientStatus = value in 500..599` excludes 408 Request Timeout and 429 Too Many Requests, which are conventionally retryable rate-limit/timeout statuses. These are classified terminal. The named cases (5xx, HttpRequestTimeoutException, IOException) ARE retried, but the broader 'transient HTTP status' coverage is narrower than the with_skill version (which adds 408/425/429).

needs_review: No CoroutineDispatcher is injected; the class is testable only via runTest's ambient scheduler, not by swapping a dispatcher.

suggestions.assertion: The HttpClient/engine and the dispatcher are INJECTED (constructor params) so the class is unit-testable (and any Clock/Random too)
suggestions.reason: This assertion is the single discriminating one between the two configs — without_skill injects HttpClient and Random but omits the dispatcher entirely. Good, sharp assertion. Worth keeping the 'and the dispatcher' clause explicit so a config that only injects the HttpClient cannot pass.

eval_feedback.overall: 6/7 pass. The one failure (dispatcher not injected) is genuine and discriminating. A secondary uncaught weakness: 408/429 are misclassified as terminal here (no assertion penalizes incomplete transient-status coverage), which a stricter retry-correctness assertion would catch.
